findings.body: The item body is saved with the raw_html cook method, whose new cook path returns raw HTML without the normal rendering/sanitization pipeline, so visitors viewing the imported topic can execute attacker-supplied JavaScript in the forum origin.
findings.evidence: creator = PostCreator.new(user, title: title, raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])
findings.failure_mode: Stored untrusted markup is rendered as active HTML in topic views.
findings.impact: The item body is saved with the raw_html cook method, whose new cook path returns raw HTML without the normal rendering/sanitization pipeline, so visitors viewing the imported topic can execute attacker-supplied JavaScript in the forum origin.
findings.root_cause: Untrusted feed content is explicitly assigned a cook method that bypasses HTML cooking and sanitization.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not mark externally supplied feed content as raw_html; pass it through the normal cooker or sanitize it with the same strict HTML allowlist before persisting/rendering it.
findings.title: Imported feed HTML bypasses the post sanitizer
findings.trigger: A configured RSS/Atom feed contains executable HTML such as a script tag or an event-handler attribute in an item body.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 22 verbatim shows `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` being passed to PostCreator. Repository context confirms `raw_html` cook method returns raw content without cooking (post.rb:133). External feed content bypasses sanitization, enabling stored XSS.

findings.body: The unescaped Referer closes the JavaScript string in the embed response and executes attacker-controlled code in the Discourse iframe origin.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted valid Referer produces reflected cross-site scripting in the embed document.
findings.impact: The unescaped Referer closes the JavaScript string in the embed response and executes attacker-controlled code in the Discourse iframe origin.
findings.root_cause: A request header is inserted into an inline JavaScript string without context-appropriate escaping.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the target origin from the parsed Referer and emit it with JSON/JavaScript escaping (for example, `origin.to_json`) rather than interpolating the raw header into a quoted script literal.
findings.title: The Referer header is interpolated into executable JavaScript
findings.trigger: An embed page is loaded from the configured host with a Referer URL containing a JavaScript string delimiter, such as a quote in an otherwise valid query string or path.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 11 verbatim shows `'<%= request.referer %>'` interpolated directly into JavaScript string. A Referer containing `'` would break out of the string literal, enabling reflected XSS in the embed page.

findings.body: The initial post for every imported thread is created at import time instead of `t[:created_at]`, changing topic chronology, ordering, and historical metadata.
findings.failure_mode: Historical imported topics receive incorrect creation timestamps.
findings.impact: The initial post for every imported thread is created at import time instead of `t[:created_at]`, changing topic chronology, ordering, and historical metadata.
findings.root_cause: The replacement import call forwards only the title and drops the existing created_at value.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the thread creation timestamp through `import_remote` and `TopicEmbed.import` to PostCreator's `created_at` option, as the previous importer did.
findings.title: Disqus imports no longer preserve the source thread creation time
findings.trigger: An administrator imports a Disqus export containing historical threads.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows line 148 calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` replacing previous `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]))`. The created_at parameter is dropped, so imported threads lose original timestamps.

findings.body: Thor rejects the previously supported option, and operators can no longer place imported threads into a selected category.
findings.evidence: method_option :category, aliases: '-c', desc: "The category to post in"
findings.failure_mode: Previously valid command-line invocations become incompatible and lose category-placement functionality.
findings.impact: Thor rejects the previously supported option, and operators can no longer place imported threads into a selected category.
findings.root_cause: The task's public category option was deleted while replacing the creation implementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the category option and propagate the resolved category into the new TopicEmbed/PostCreator import path.
findings.title: The documented Disqus category option was removed
findings.trigger: Existing import automation invokes the Disqus Thor task with `--category` or `-c`.
findings.verifier_reason: LEFT source line 117 shows `method_option :category` was removed in the patch. This breaks existing automation using `--category` flag and removes category placement functionality.

raw_findings.body: Path-relative URLs are left relative to the Discourse topic rather than the source article, while protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to the source host; imported links and images therefore point to incorrect locations.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Imported content contains broken or misdirected links and assets.
raw_findings.impact: Path-relative URLs are left relative to the Discourse topic rather than the source article, while protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to the source host; imported links and images therefore point to incorrect locations.
raw_findings.root_cause: The URL normalizer only recognizes values beginning with `/` and constructs replacements from a host prefix instead of applying standard URI resolution.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Resolve each non-absolute href/src with `URI.join(url, value)` (while preserving fragment-only and already-absolute URLs) for both anchors and images.
raw_findings.title: Relative imported URLs are resolved incorrectly
raw_findings.trigger: An imported article contains a path-relative URL such as `href="next.html"` or a protocol-relative asset URL such as `src="//cdn.example/image.png"`.

raw_findings.body: The layout references `embed.css`, but the explicit asset precompile list does not include the new embed bundle, so the stylesheet is absent from the compiled assets (or raises an asset-not-precompiled error depending on asset configuration).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Embed pages render without their stylesheet or fail asset resolution in production.
raw_findings.impact: The layout references `embed.css`, but the explicit asset precompile list does not include the new embed bundle, so the stylesheet is absent from the compiled assets (or raises an asset-not-precompiled error depending on asset configuration).
raw_findings.root_cause: A newly referenced standalone asset was added without registering it in this application's explicit production precompile configuration.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `embed.css` to `config.assets.precompile` (and add `embed.js` as well if it is intended to be served as an asset).
raw_findings.title: Embed stylesheet is not included in the production precompile set
raw_findings.trigger: The application is deployed with normal production asset compilation and an embed page is requested.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Derive the target origin from the parsed Referer and emit it with JSON/JavaScript escaping (for example, `origin.to_json`) rather than interpolating the raw header into a quoted script literal.
validated_findings.title: The Referer header is interpolated into executable JavaScript
validated_findings.trigger: An embed page is loaded from the configured host with a Referer URL containing a JavaScript string delimiter, such as a quote in an otherwise valid query string or path.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 11 verbatim shows `'<%= request.referer %>'` interpolated directly into JavaScript string. A Referer containing `'` would break out of the string literal, enabling reflected XSS in the embed page.

validated_findings.body: Path-relative URLs are left relative to the Discourse topic rather than the source article, while protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to the source host; imported links and images therefore point to incorrect locations.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Imported content contains broken or misdirected links and assets.
validated_findings.impact: Path-relative URLs are left relative to the Discourse topic rather than the source article, while protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to the source host; imported links and images therefore point to incorrect locations.
validated_findings.root_cause: The URL normalizer only recognizes values beginning with `/` and constructs replacements from a host prefix instead of applying standard URI resolution.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Resolve each non-absolute href/src with `URI.join(url, value)` (while preserving fragment-only and already-absolute URLs) for both anchors and images.
validated_findings.title: Relative imported URLs are resolved incorrectly
validated_findings.trigger: An imported article contains a path-relative URL such as `href="next.html"` or a protocol-relative asset URL such as `src="//cdn.example/image.png"`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 64 shows `href.start_with?('/')` check. Path-relative URLs like `href="next.html"` don't start with `/` and are left unchanged, becoming relative to Discourse topic URL. Protocol-relative `//cdn.example` also starts with `/` and gets incorrectly prefixed.

validated_findings.body: The layout references `embed.css`, but the explicit asset precompile list does not include the new embed bundle, so the stylesheet is absent from the compiled assets (or raises an asset-not-precompiled error depending on asset configuration).
validated_findings.failure_mode: Embed pages render without their stylesheet or fail asset resolution in production.
validated_findings.impact: The layout references `embed.css`, but the explicit asset precompile list does not include the new embed bundle, so the stylesheet is absent from the compiled assets (or raises an asset-not-precompiled error depending on asset configuration).
validated_findings.root_cause: A newly referenced standalone asset was added without registering it in this application's explicit production precompile configuration.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `embed.css` to `config.assets.precompile` (and add `embed.js` as well if it is intended to be served as an asset).
validated_findings.title: Embed stylesheet is not included in the production precompile set
validated_findings.trigger: The application is deployed with normal production asset compilation and an embed page is requested.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that embed.css is missing from precompile is speculative. Rails asset pipeline may auto-compile stylesheets referenced via stylesheet_link_tag. No evidence in patch that this causes actual failure; config/application.rb shows precompile patterns that may include it.

validated_findings.body: The initial post for every imported thread is created at import time instead of `t[:created_at]`, changing topic chronology, ordering, and historical metadata.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Historical imported topics receive incorrect creation timestamps.
validated_findings.impact: The initial post for every imported thread is created at import time instead of `t[:created_at]`, changing topic chronology, ordering, and historical metadata.
validated_findings.root_cause: The replacement import call forwards only the title and drops the existing created_at value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the thread creation timestamp through `import_remote` and `TopicEmbed.import` to PostCreator's `created_at` option, as the previous importer did.
validated_findings.title: Disqus imports no longer preserve the source thread creation time
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator imports a Disqus export containing historical threads.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows line 148 calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` replacing previous `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]))`. The created_at parameter is dropped, so imported threads lose original timestamps.

validated_findings.body: Thor rejects the previously supported option, and operators can no longer place imported threads into a selected category.
validated_findings.evidence: method_option :category, aliases: '-c', desc: "The category to post in"
validated_findings.failure_mode: Previously valid command-line invocations become incompatible and lose category-placement functionality.
validated_findings.impact: Thor rejects the previously supported option, and operators can no longer place imported threads into a selected category.
validated_findings.root_cause: The task's public category option was deleted while replacing the creation implementation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Retain the category option and propagate the resolved category into the new TopicEmbed/PostCreator import path.
validated_findings.title: The documented Disqus category option was removed
validated_findings.trigger: Existing import automation invokes the Disqus Thor task with `--category` or `-c`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: LEFT source line 117 shows `method_option :category` was removed in the patch. This breaks existing automation using `--category` flag and removes category placement functionality.

validated_findings.body: The foreign page passes the origin check and can set the legitimate Discourse iframe's height, enabling UI corruption or denial of service on pages containing the embed script.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Messages from an unrelated origin are treated as trusted iframe resize events.
validated_findings.impact: The foreign page passes the origin check and can set the legitimate Discourse iframe's height, enabling UI corruption or denial of service on pages containing the embed script.
validated_findings.root_cause: The message listener uses substring containment rather than exact origin and source-window validation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compare `e.origin` exactly with the parsed origin of discourseUrl and also require `e.source === iframe.contentWindow` before processing a resize message.
validated_findings.title: Resize messages accept origins based on substring matching
validated_findings.trigger: The configured Discourse URL has a host such as `forum.example.co.uk` and a page from the distinct origin `https://forum.example.co` sends a message to an embedding page; that origin is a substring of the configured URL.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 17 shows `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` which is substring matching. If discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.co.uk`, origin `https://forum.example.co` passes the check, allowing foreign origins to send resize messages.
